## Synth-Rock: `aliens_counting.yml`

A mid-eighties synth-rock anthem in the manner of The Final Countdown, with a fanfare of its own in
sixteenths on synth brass, over power chords, a pad and a rock beat with crashes.

<a id="annandale"></a>
## Jazz-Rock: `annandale.yml`

A seventies jazz-rock song in the manner of Steely Dan's My Old School, lightly swung: an electric
piano on the scale chord 7, so that the Progression gives each chord the seventh its scale says, and
a horn line answered two scale steps below by a transposed second horn track.

<a id="green_men"></a>
## Pop-Punk Strumming: `green_men.yml`

A pop-punk song in the manner of Green Day and Sum 41 at 180 beats a minute. The guitar track strums
every power chord down, tight, as a pick rakes the strings, and in the bridge a Strum generator in
the clips' chains wins over the track's strum and rakes down and up, looser.

<a id="know_your_slang"></a>
## Indie Rock: `know_your_slang.yml`

An indie rock song in two moods after the Shins' New Slang and Know Your Onion, with melodies of its
own: a strummed acoustic guitar with a tambourine, then a jangling electric guitar and a full kit.
The acoustic guitar's track strums down and up.

<a id="not_werewolves"></a>
## Outlaw Piano Rock: `not_werewolves.yml`

An upbeat honky-tonk piano rock song on the chords of Warren Zevon's Frank and Jesse James, in its
key of F major, with a melody and a solo of its own. It opens like saloon music, a stride left hand
under a ragtime right hand, before the band comes in and the upright piano plays the tune in
octaves, with a ragtime solo and a quiet ballad scene before the last chorus.

<a id="training_montage"></a>
## Arena-Rock: `training_montage.yml`

An early-eighties film anthem in the manner of Eye of the Tiger, for a training montage: muted
guitar chords hit in a syncopated rhythm with the kick, then a driving rock beat and a brass lead.
The rhythm and the melody are its own.

<a id="volcano"></a>
## Guitar Showpiece: `volcano.yml`

A solo guitar showpiece in the manner of Van Halen's Eruption: the band hits a chord and leaves the
guitar alone for runs in thirty-second notes, a trill, and tapped arpeggios, a held chord broken up
by an arpeggiator in sixteenth-note triplets.
